subject: Trial pool briefing + procurement path for Vervana Health
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditi Shah <aditi.shah@vervanahealth.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@vervanahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Trial pool briefing + procurement path for Vervana Health

Hi Aditi / Tom —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap so we’re aligned and can move the trial/procurement work forward. If I missed anything please flag.

High-level ask from Vervana: evaluate a single-tenant reserved GPU pool for inference of clinical-NLP models (PHI in scope) with predictable p95 latency and a clear procurement path to a multi-month reserved commitment if the trial meets throughput/latency targets.

Key pain points and constraints you shared
- PHI-handling: data stays in VPC, customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) required, SOC2/HIPAA compliance evidence needed for procurement.
- Latency sensitivity: triage API calls for clinical UIs — target interactive latency at p95 under 250ms for the standard LLM path.
- Predictability: spikes during batch-annotation windows; need burst policy but no noisy neighbors during core hours.
- Cost predictability: procurement team needs a clear monthly commit figure for budgeting.

Proposed trial configuration (what we discussed)
- Trial duration: 6 weeks (recommended)
- Reserved pool: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs in a single-tenant pool (isolated tenant lane)
- Burst: configured burst to shared capacity up to +2 GPUs for non-core hours
- Autoscaling: constrained to maintain lane isolation; scaling rules attached in the playbook.
- SLO targets: throughput ~40 reqs/s for your typical 512-token sessions; p95 latency <= 250ms.

Security & networking checklist (to unblock setup)
1) VPC peering or PrivateLink (you preferred VPC peering)
2) KMS key provisioning and IAM role for Redwood to write logs to your audit bucket
3) SOC2 evidence: we’ll share the security pack and a SOC2 attestation PDF (attached)

Procurement path & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): sign an MSA addendum + Non-production trial PO (estimate provided in attached doc).
- Week 1: infra provisioning & VPC networking; Redwood ops runs connectivity test.
- Week 2: model import, validation, and baseline perf run.
- Weeks 3–6: trial operations, daily dashboards for token/latency economics, weekly checkpoints.

Requested next steps (for Aditi / Tom to confirm)
- Approve the 6-week trial & tentative reserve (4 GPUs) so we can route the PO to billing.
- Share your procurement contact and preferred PO format (vendor details attached).
- Confirm timeline availability week of Jul 5 for network setup call with Marissa (ops).

Attachments: ver vana-sla-draft-v1.pdf (SLA + trial terms), isolation-topology.png (network sketch)

Thanks — I’ll draft the addendum and the PO estimate once you confirm the trial size.

Cheers,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Trial pool briefing + procurement path for Vervana Health

Thanks Ben — this is helpful and matches our notes. A few clarifications from procurement/infra: 

1) Trial size: procurement wants a breakdown of unit economics per-GPU (hourly and estimated monthly committed rate) so they can evaluate against an internal benchmark. Can you include a small table in the PO estimate showing per-GPU effective cost at 50% and 80% utilization?

2) Isolation: we need confirmation that logs and KV caches aren’t shared outside our tenant lane. You mentioned prefix-based KV caching — can you confirm it's strictly tenant-isolated for the trial?

3) SLA ask: procurement will accept a 99.5% uptime target for the trial window; full SLA negotiation will follow for a multi-month commit. Any rollback or fallback behavior if the lane saturates? Please call out automated fallback (lower-cost model or queued requests) and who owns user-facing errors.

Procurement contact: Priya Iyer <priya.iyer@vervanahealth.com> (cc’ing here would be Priya but she’s OOO until Jul 1). We’ll either route a small trial PO through her or share vendor onboarding docs.

We can do the network setup call on Tue Jul 6 at 10am PT — Marissa, can you confirm?

Aditi
Director of ML Ops
Vervana Health
aditi.shah@vervanahealth.com

Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Trial pool briefing + procurement path for Vervana Health

Appreciate the quick clarifications — answers inline and a short action list below. Quoting Aditi for context: 

> 1) Trial size: procurement wants a breakdown of unit economics per-GPU (hourly and estimated monthly committed rate) so they can evaluate against an internal benchmark. Can you include a small table in the PO estimate showing per-GPU effective cost at 50% and 80% utilization?

Yes — I’ll include a per-GPU cost table in the PO estimate showing: list price/hour, effective $/token at your 512-token median, and the committed-rate equivalents at 50% / 80% utilization. Expect that in the PO doc I’ll send by end of day Mon Jun 28.

> 2) Isolation: we need confirmation that logs and KV caches aren’t shared outside our tenant lane. You mentioned prefix-based KV caching — can you confirm it's strictly tenant-isolated for the trial?

Confirmed — tenant lane isolation enforces separate KV namespaces and logging buckets. During the trial we’ll provision a tenant-specific KV prefix and a dedicated log bucket in your account (or a customer-managed bucket). I’ve asked Marissa (ops) to include the network/KMS checklist on the setup call.

> 3) SLA ask: procurement will accept a 99.5% uptime target for the trial window; full SLA negotiation will follow for a multi-month commit. Any rollback or fallback behavior if the lane saturates? Please call out automated fallback (lower-cost model or queued requests) and who owns user-facing errors.

Fallback behavior: by default we will route excess traffic to a preconfigured fallback model (compatible but smaller) and emit explanatory error codes for callers. Redwood willown the fallback routing; your app remains responsible for surface-level messaging to end users. For the trial we’ll log all fallback events and include them in the weekly report.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Ben: Draft PO estimate with per-GPU economics + attached SLA by Mon 2027-06-28 EOD.
- Marissa: Ops to schedule network setup call on Tue 2027-07-06 at 10am PT; prepare VPC peering checklist and KMS steps.
- Aditi/Priya: Confirm preferred PO format (vendor PO vs. one-time invoice) and provide procurement contact details if different from Priya.
- Tom: Share example peak traffic traces so we can validate burst sizing (optional, helpful).

If that looks right I’ll queue the trial provisioning once we have a signed PO. Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales – Redwood Inference
